rule: GOAL: Fill the four empty slots with the specific colors shown in the top row, in that exact order. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette to select it, then click a slot to place it. RULE: The top row displays the required sequence; matching this order is the only way to win. TRAP: Assuming the order of colors does not matter or that the bottom palette order is the target.

GOAL: Reach the far corner tile to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move you two spaces at a time. RULE: You only stop on clear tiles; walls block the path. TRAP: Believing you move one space per press wastes time.

GOAL: Move the purple square to the blue planet. CONTROLS: Click a dot to slide the square one step in that direction. RULE: You must land on the dots to move; the square stops at the target. TRAP: Thinking the plus sign was a goal; it was just a tutorial hint.

GOAL: Guide the falling beam to the target using the paddle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the paddle; Space fires the beam. RULE: The paddle splits the beam: one part travels right to the wall, the other shifts left before falling. TRAP: Believing the beam falls off the paddle's edge. It does not; the rightward beam continues horizontally to the wall.

GOAL: Shift the gray block to align the yellow plug with the wall gap. CONTROLS: Top blue button moves the upper edge left and lower edge right; bottom button reverses this. RULE: Only the two blue buttons move the block; other clicks do nothing. TRAP: Wasting time probing inactive areas instead of testing the blue buttons immediately.

GOAL: Slide the green plug to align with the gap in the black wall. CONTROLS: Click buttons to shift the horizontal bands left or right. RULE: Moving one band in a direction shifts the adjacent bands the opposite way. TRAP: Assuming buttons only move their own band; they affect neighbors too.

GOAL: Grab three specific blocks and pull them into the box using a grappling rope. CONTROLS: Arrows move the character; the rope extends to catch blocks and retracts to drag them. RULE: Attached blocks move rigidly with the box, so you must align your height before grabbing. TRAP: Moving up while dragging blocks causes fatal collisions if they overlap other objects during the shift.

GOAL: Reach the exit by navigating around a lethal, lunging guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in the chosen direction. RULE: The guard attacks horizontally when you are adjacent; never share a row with it during its turn. TRAP: Believing you can safely step onto the guard’s tile to collect it; contact is always fatal, requiring you to find a vertical path instead.

GOAL: Rotate five glyph columns to match the target symbols shown above them. CONTROLS: Arrows shift focus left or right between columns; UP rotates the selected glyph. RULE: Each column cycles through a fixed sequence of symbols; count the steps needed to reach the target. TRAP: Believing every column shares the same rotation cycle or direction, leading to wasted presses.

GOAL: Navigate to the exit while collecting items and eliminating guards to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Guards only attack along their facing line of sight, leaving perpendicular paths safe. TRAP: Assuming guards attack in all directions wastes time; they ignore perpendicular approaches.

GOAL: Merge two small shapes into a larger one and place it onto the target circle. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the selected piece toward the cursor until it hits an obstacle or merges. RULE: Pieces only combine when their edges touch; the merged shape takes the position of the moving piece. TRAP: Assuming the merged shape centers on the click point instead of anchoring to the original piece’s corner.

GOAL: Place the third box into the designated gap to complete the puzzle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character, while SPACE attaches or detaches boxes when facing them directly. RULE: Boxes stick to the side you are facing, requiring you to reorient before releasing them. TRAP: Pressing SPACE while facing a different direction than the box fails to detach it, wasting turns.

GOAL: Shrink the marker to fit the narrow channel and slide it into the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the marker; submissions clear the grid and reduce marker size. RULE: The marker must match the channel's width to pass through to the socket. TRAP: Assuming all grid cells must be cleared was irrelevant; size reduction was the key.

GOAL: Align the shrinking marker with the handle to complete the connection. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; clicks transfer it to the upper chamber. RULE: The marker jumps to the top chamber upon transfer, bypassing the narrow channel. TRAP: Assuming you must manually navigate the tight corridor after shrinking, rather than relying on the automatic transfer.

GOAL: Move colored bars to align under cup notches for dropping. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected bar; mouse selects a bar; space drops all. RULE: Bars must sit directly under the empty notch column to fall into the cup. TRAP: Assuming any alignment works; precise column matching with the gap is required.

GOAL: Align the plug with the socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click switches to toggle their state; click the plug to insert it. RULE: All switches must be set to the correct pattern before insertion. TRAP: Assuming the plug moves automatically; it requires a manual click to insert.

GOAL: Fill specific gaps in tall walls using liquid from adjacent bands without overflowing caps. CONTROLS: Click wall sides to transfer liquid; observe height changes. RULE: Liquid cannot rise above the shortest adjacent wall’s height. TRAP: Assuming you can drain any band to zero; some bands have hidden floors or caps blocking flow.

GOAL: Arrange three tokens by swapping their positions. CONTROLS: Click a token to select it; click another to swap them. Clicking a selected token deselects it. Press space to finalize the move. RULE: Selections are mutually exclusive; clicking a new token replaces the active selection instead of adding to it. TRAP: Believing empty clicks deselect tokens. They do nothing, leaving the previous selection active and causing unintended swaps.

GOAL: Fill seven empty slots to match the top color sequence, ignoring the pre-marked colored frames. CONTROLS: Click a palette color to select it, then click a slot to place it. Press Space to submit the full grid. RULE: The colored frames inside the main box act as dividers, forcing the sequence to flow through the side boxes in specific segments. TRAP: Assuming you can fill slots in any order or skip the side boxes causes immediate failure; you must follow the segmented path.

GOAL: Align the hollow gate frame with the red box’s third slot to resolve the color index sequence. CONTROLS: Click to select the gate, then click the target slot to place it; press space to confirm the solution. RULE: The gate occupies no position in the reading order, so the green box tokens immediately follow the red tokens preceding the gate. TRAP: Believing the gate consumes a slot index, which shifts the expected color positions and breaks the sequence logic.

GOAL: Route three balls into matching cups by splitting their paths. CONTROLS: Click to place or remove barriers; arrow keys adjust positions; spacebar launches balls. RULE: Balls split when hitting a barrier's edge, sending half-pieces in both directions along the barrier's length. TRAP: Assuming off-board exits were harmless, when they actually counted as failures, requiring precise barrier alignment to keep all split pieces on-screen.

GOAL: Place colored tokens into red slots while positioning gates to separate specific color groups. CONTROLS: Click to pick up tokens or gates, then click again to drop them into open slots. Press Space to verify the solution. RULE: Blue tokens must be grouped in triples that match the reading order of the blue display box. TRAP: Assuming gates could separate overlapping token groups; they must sit in distinct slots between non-overlapping triples.

GOAL: Route the beam to the pink target by navigating around the charcoal gate. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the marker; the marker fires a beam in its facing direction. RULE: The beam travels straight through open space but stops at the gate, requiring precise alignment. TRAP: Believing the beam could destroy the gate or that marker size indicated remaining moves.

GOAL: Decode the hidden sequence to assign the correct color gates and matching tokens to each box. CONTROLS: Drag gates to the red slots to define reading order, place tokens in the colored boxes, and press space to verify. RULE: The left-to-right order of gates in the red box dictates which colored box corresponds to each segment of the sequence. TRAP: Assuming gates are just labels rather than ordering keys, or misaligning token pairs with the wrong gate color.

GOAL: Align two colored crosshairs to cover all matching target dots on the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected crosshair; Spacebar switches control between the yellow and blue crosshairs. RULE: A target is cleared only when its center dot is directly covered by the active crosshair’s lines. TRAP: Assuming a single crosshair could clear all targets; failing to switch selection leaves half the puzzle unsolved.

GOAL: Extend the yellow bar until it touches the red plus sign. CONTROLS: Click the bottom yellow marker to lengthen the bar toward the right. RULE: The bar grows in fixed increments and stops when adjacent to the target object. TRAP: Trying to overlap the plus sign wastes moves; stop the moment the bar reaches it.

GOAL: Align three colored cursors with matching target dots to clear the board. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cursor; Space switches to the next cursor. RULE: Each cursor only covers targets of its own specific color. TRAP: Moving the wrong color cursor wastes actions; always verify the active color before moving.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align the single yellow block with the yellow bracket. CONTROLS: Red arrow rotates the ring counter-clockwise; green arrow rotates it clockwise. RULE: Only the yellow block matters; ignore all other colored tiles while rotating. TRAP: Clicking the green arrow moves the yellow block away from the target, wasting time.

GOAL: Align the block’s color pattern with the target icon by rotating it correctly. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block; landing on the plus tile rotated the piece. RULE: The bottom-left icon displays the current rotation state, which must match the top target. TRAP: Assuming the block itself visually rotated; only the orientation indicator changed, confusing the state check.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single remaining peg by eliminating all others. CONTROLS: Click a peg to highlight valid landing spots, then click a spot to jump over an adjacent peg into it. RULE: Moves are strict orthogonal jumps over exactly one neighbor into an empty space, removing the jumped peg. TRAP: Assuming any empty space is a valid target; only highlighted rings indicate legal moves, so blind clicks waste actions.

GOAL: Move the dark token into the left slot while the white token stays in the right. CONTROLS: Click a token to select it; arrows shift the selected token by one grid unit. RULE: Only the selected token moves; the other remains stationary until clicked. TRAP: Assuming both tokens move together or that clicking swaps positions instead of control.

GOAL: Clear the grid by matching all colored cells correctly. CONTROLS: Click individual cells to rotate or select them for alignment. RULE: Only clicks on specific center markers trigger state changes; empty clicks just blink. TRAP: Believing every cell click works wastes time; precise targeting is essential.

GOAL: Move three shapes to cover all red targets. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active shape; Space cycles selection. RULE: Each press moves the shape exactly three cells. TRAP: Assuming targets are covered only by centers; edges also count.

GOAL: Make the grid's pattern match the two marker masks. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color. RULE: Each marker dictates the specific colors of the surrounding grid cells. TRAP: Assuming markers were toggleable or that clicking affected adjacent cells.

GOAL: Move the head to the exact center of the black shape. CONTROLS: Click a cell to place the head there; click the tail to swap positions. RULE: The midpoint of the head and tail must land on the target center. TRAP: Believing you can move the tail independently; it only moves when swapped.

GOAL: Merge the two separate blocks into a single unit by moving them into the same cell. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both blocks simultaneously in the pressed direction. RULE: Blocks slide until they hit a wall or another block; overlapping is required to win. TRAP: Believing blocks must merely touch is wrong; they must fully occupy the same space.

GOAL: Move two yellow tiles into the bracketed corners. CONTROLS: Click red buttons to shift specific rows or columns of the grid. RULE: Yellow tiles are the only pieces that matter; other colors are just visual noise. TRAP: Wasting time analyzing non-yellow tiles or trying to predict complex row shifts instead of focusing on yellow paths.

GOAL: Move two blocks into a single shared cell to merge them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide both blocks simultaneously in that direction. RULE: A block stops if the next tile is blocked, a wall, or a hazard. TRAP: Assuming both blocks move equal distances; one may halt early, leaving the other to slide further.

GOAL: Match the grid pattern to the correct color rule for all four markers. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle between red and orange. RULE: White cells take the opposite color of the marker, while gray cells take the marker's color. TRAP: Assuming white cells match the marker's color like earlier levels, which creates a consistent but wrong solution.

GOAL: Place the yellow block in the yellow bracket and the orange block in the orange bracket. CONTROLS: Left arrows rotate the left ring; right arrows rotate the right ring. RULE: Blocks must match the color of their target bracket, not just any empty slot. TRAP: Assuming any filled slot counts as a win wastes actions on swapped, invalid placements.

GOAL: Move the plus symbol to overlap the orange square and trigger a color change. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the plus symbol one step per press. RULE: Overlapping the target shape with sufficient depth caused the required reaction. TRAP: Assuming a single edge pixel overlap was enough wasted time; deeper alignment was necessary.

GOAL: Deliver a peg from the cart into the small board’s target slot. CONTROLS: Click to move the cart; click objects to interact. RULE: Only the cart can transfer pegs; static pegs cannot move. TRAP: Believing the fixed peg could be pushed or removed wasted time.

ESTABLISHED: The player starts blue at the top-left. The board resets to this state when a key is pressed. A gray trail appears behind the player only in the second visual mode. FAILED: Moving without toggling the mode creates no trail and fails to trigger any goal state. Repeatedly restarting without changing the mode yields identical results. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching a specific tile while in the first mode, nor is it about the color of the starting blob. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blob. The spacebar resets the level position and toggles the visual mode between plain and trail-enabled.

GOAL: Color all cells to satisfy hidden constraints using the three-color palette. CONTROLS: Clicking cycles a cell’s color through the available options. RULE: The rule “gray means not equal to the center color” was the key to solving the grid. TRAP: Assuming gray cells matched the center color wasted time before realizing they had to be different.

GOAL: Fill four empty slots with matching blocks. CONTROLS: Click to grab a block; arrows move it. RULE: Only blocks with identical dimensions fit their slots. TRAP: Assuming any block fits if it looks small enough, ignoring exact width and height matches.

GOAL: Place the yellow and orange tokens into their matching brackets. CONTROLS: Click arrows to shift tokens along two large loops, one horizontal and one vertical, which intersect at four points. RULE: Tokens follow the loops strictly, jumping across empty gaps to the next slot in the cycle. TRAP: Assuming tokens stop at empty spaces or move only to adjacent cells wastes time; they wrap around the entire loop.

GOAL: Rotate the block 180 degrees to match the box icon before entering it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block across the grid, triggering effects upon entry. RULE: Plus tiles are permanent; leaving and re-entering rotates the block again for each pass. TRAP: Believing plus tiles vanish after one use, which prevents achieving the required double rotation.

GOAL: Grow the sky bar upward to reach the target height. CONTROLS: Click a bar to extend its length in a specific direction. RULE: Bars grow only into empty space and stop if they hit a wall. TRAP: Assuming bars grow symmetrically; they extend from the head, so direction matters.

GOAL: Position both diamond knots onto their matching colored rings. CONTROLS: Click a cell to swap diamond colors; drag a diamond to move it along its chain. RULE: A knot is the geometric center of three connected same-color diamonds. TRAP: Assuming rings block movement; diamonds can safely overlap ring visuals without triggering a fail state.

GOAL: Place two yellow blocks into the top bracket slots. CONTROLS: Red clicks rotate a central ring; arrows spin the top row. RULE: The ring is a single 21-cell loop, not two separate circles. TRAP: Assuming the ring splits into two cycles wastes time on false theories.

GOAL: Slide the dark block onto the glowing yellow outline. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to shift the entire block one step at a time. RULE: The yellow shape is a ghost target, not a solid wall, so blocks can pass through it. TRAP: Avoiding the yellow area caused wasted moves; overlapping the target is safe and necessary.

GOAL: Solve both colored knots to clear the board. CONTROLS: Click tiles to move pieces or swap positions. RULE: The knot forms exactly at the midpoint between two matching colored slots. TRAP: Assuming one solved knot ends the level; you must solve every color to win.

GOAL: Nest three colored boxes to build a seven-item sequence that reads Red, Blue, Yellow, Green, Green, Blue, Red. CONTROLS: Drag colored blocks and gate tokens into empty slots within the red, blue, and green boxes. Press Space to verify the final order. RULE: Placing a gate token into a slot inserts the referenced box’s contents at that position, allowing deep nesting. TRAP: Trying to place items side-by-side fails because only one nested structure yields the correct seven-item length and center Yellow.

GOAL: Force specific tiles to white while restoring other cells to navy. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color; pressing a tile toggles it and its neighbors. RULE: Tile presses ripple outward, so undo unwanted neighbor changes with single clicks. TRAP: Thinking tile presses only affect themselves ignores the cross-shaped spread.

GOAL: Place the purple shape directly beneath the white block, aligned and touching. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the piece's position; mouse clicks select the purple color. RULE: The target panel shows the purple piece immediately below the white block with no gap. TRAP: Thinking the piece could be pushed into place; rotation alone determines position.

GOAL: Align the black shape's mirror image exactly over the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space toggles control between the divider and the black shape. RULE: The divider defines the mirror axis, so its position dictates the reflected shape's location. TRAP: Believing moving the black shape alone suffices, ignoring that the divider must shift to fix horizontal alignment.

GOAL: Move the green player to the yellow token by navigating rotating bars and moving platforms. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; clicking colored buttons rotates or swaps the corresponding bar and checker. RULE: Only stand on the dark red anchor when rotating bars, or you will be carried to a new position. TRAP: Assuming you can walk through the red bar after rotating it; you must wait for the blue checker to clear the path above.

GOAL: Move three symbols to specific spots to recolor target zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active symbol; Space switches to the next symbol in the cycle. RULE: A symbol recolors a zone only if its path touches that zone exactly once. TRAP: Assuming you can touch a zone multiple times or cross paths without penalty costs extra moves.

GOAL: Clear the level by guiding the player through a vertical shaft to reach the top room. CONTROLS: Use mouse clicks to remove obstacles; use arrow keys to move the player horizontally. RULE: The player automatically rises when the path directly above is clear of blocks. TRAP: Believing you must move the player sideways to trigger the rise; simply removing the blocking block above is enough to start the ascent.

GOAL: Route three independent diamond chains to their target zones. CONTROLS: Click a slot to swap the white diamond in; click a destination to move it. RULE: A chain is solved when the average position of all its diamonds lands on the target knot. TRAP: Assuming the final position is the only constraint; intermediate moves must also keep every diamond separated from others.

GOAL: Move two blocks to marked zones while adjusting a full-width divider’s height. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block or divider; Space cycles selection. RULE: The divider must be positioned between the blocks’ final rows, requiring careful sequencing of moves to avoid blocking paths. TRAP: Assuming blocks and dividers cannot overlap; they can pass through each other, which simplifies routing.

ESTABLISHED: The socket moves in 3-unit increments. The plug moves horizontally. Alignment depends on precise vertical positioning relative to the socket's pins. FAILED: Inserting the plug and clicking either object to change states did not trigger a win. Moving the socket without restoring its original position failed. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing the plug anywhere near the socket or toggling colors while misaligned. CONTROLS: Click objects to toggle lock states. Use directional keys to move unlocked objects in discrete steps.

GOAL: Cover two yellow crosses using two black shapes and their mirrored reflections across the central divider. CONTROLS: Arrows move and rotate shapes; space confirms placement or triggers reflection. RULE: Each cross is fully filled only when a shape’s placement aligns perfectly with its reflection across the axis. TRAP: Assuming shapes cover crosses independently; ignoring reflection symmetry leads to mismatched gaps and wasted moves.

GOAL: Move the yellow piece to the north slot of the blue ring. CONTROLS: Click arrows to rotate rings and shift pieces along the circular track. RULE: Each ring rotates only in one fixed direction; you cannot reverse it directly. TRAP: Assuming all rings spin the same way; the blue ring spun opposite to the others, forcing a long detour.

GOAL: Shift two lower bars left to open gaps, letting falling blocks drop through without splitting into unwanted numbers. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected bar; spacebar drops all blocks. RULE: Blocks only pass through empty columns; hitting a solid bar splits them into adjacent values. TRAP: Thinking bars could be stacked vertically to block paths; they must be aligned horizontally to create a single continuous gap.

GOAL: Align two yellow tiles into specific slots by cycling colored tiles through overlapping loops. CONTROLS: Clicks rotated connected tile groups, with some clicks shifting multiple loops simultaneously. RULE: Yellow tiles stay trapped in their starting loops; only shared corner tiles transfer between paths. TRAP: Believing clicks act independently; in fact, rotating one loop forces the linked loop to rotate too, coupling their movements.

GOAL: Color specific grid cells purple and orange by pushing colored bands across the board. CONTROLS: Arrows move bands, Space rotates, Clicks confirm placement. RULE: Bands slide until hitting edges, leaving permanent color trails that define the final shape. TRAP: Assuming diagonal bands cover all corner cells; they often miss extreme corners due to fixed width limits.

GOAL: Move the green token to the square and slide both pluses into their matching slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green token; pushing a plus shifts it one cell in that direction. RULE: Pluses only move when the green token pushes them; the token cannot move through them. TRAP: Believing the token can slide over a plus; it blocks movement, forcing you to push instead.

GOAL: Build a two-tone ring by swapping entry pieces and absorbing color pairs to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click to move a diamond piece, click a slot to swap contents, or click a knot to absorb an adjacent blob. RULE: A knot absorbs a blob only if its half-colors align, merging them into a larger chain with a new central knot. TRAP: Assuming overlapping a ring prevents movement; diamonds can slide over ring arcs without triggering a collision error.

GOAL: Cover the yellow pinwheel pattern by placing a shape and its rotated copy. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the shape; clicks rotated it. RULE: Dividers reflected the shape across the grid center, creating the required symmetry. TRAP: Assuming reflections overlapped perfectly. Extra blocks stuck out, but only covering yellow mattered, not exact alignment.

GOAL: Reach the exit in two moves by removing the guard blocking the path. CONTROLS: Use directional arrows to move the player one step at a time. RULE: Moving onto a guard from the side removes it instantly. TRAP: Assuming you must fight or wait for the guard; simply walking into its flank clears the way.

GOAL: Move the notch to the target slot. CONTROLS: Click boxes to shift the notch. RULE: The notch moves in the direction it opens; hitting an edge rotates it ninety degrees. TRAP: Thinking boxes merely toggle between two fixed spots instead of rotating the notch based on its opening direction.

GOAL: Deliver two separate pieces to their respective target circles. CONTROLS: Click a destination to slide a selected piece up to a fixed maximum distance. RULE: A piece is delivered when its center lands inside the target circle’s boundary. TRAP: Assuming the piece must fully cover the circle; partial overlap with the center inside is sufficient.

GOAL: Fit three colored tokens into matching slots without blocking exits. CONTROLS: Arrows slide tokens until they hit walls or other pieces. Clicks rotate tokens in place. RULE: Tokens only move when the path is completely clear; they cannot pass through gaps in other pieces. TRAP: Assuming a token slides all the way to the far wall, ignoring that intermediate pieces stop movement early.

GOAL: Reach the exit while dodging orange patrollers. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; wait in place to adjust timing. RULE: Patrollers block specific cells at specific times; you must arrive when they are gone. TRAP: Rushing the direct path causes collisions; taking a longer detour is often faster.

GOAL: Push the orange block into the right-side slot to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your green character; pushing blocks moves them. RULE: Approach the block from the right to push it left into the target. TRAP: Approaching from the left triggers a piston ejection mechanism, wasting moves.

GOAL: Slide the dividers to position the reflection bands correctly. CONTROLS: Click a divider to select it; arrow keys move the selected piece. RULE: A divider is active when its handle dots turn white. TRAP: Clicking an already-white handle registers as a no-op, stalling input until a valid move follows.

ESTABLISHED: Red zone strictly follows diagonal i+j>=9. Orange block occupies rows 0-2, cols 3-6. Green chip is at column 47. FAILED: Rotating to East and pushing green chip without verifying slot orientation first, leading to wasted moves. GOAL IS NOT: A simple diagonal split; the orange block position is critical for future coverage. CONTROLS: UP rotates SE to E. SPACE pushes selected chip.

GOAL: Paint the grid with specific color regions using directional pushes. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the push direction, clicks select colors, and space executes the push. RULE: Pushes paint all cells satisfying a geometric condition relative to the chosen direction. TRAP: Assuming rotations follow a simple linear path rather than a circular orbit.

GOAL: Move the piece to the West slot and push the blue chip to paint the left side. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece; number keys select chips; Space pushes; clicking the mini paints. RULE: Movement snaps to the adjacent slot with the strongest directional displacement; weak shifts are ignored. TRAP: Assuming diagonal slots allow horizontal moves; from the bottom, only the vertical shift counts, blocking leftward input.

GOAL: Reach the yellow token by navigating around a rotating barrier to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one space; clicking rotated the central bar. RULE: Clicking the red button rotated the horizontal bar into a vertical column, opening the path to the target. TRAP: Assuming the bar’s rotation direction mattered; its symmetry meant the outcome was identical regardless of turn direction.

GOAL: Clear the grid by removing guards without triggering their attacks. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to move the player one step in a direction. RULE: Guards only lunge along their visible dot axis, not sideways or diagonally. TRAP: Assuming guards attack in all directions wastes moves; move perpendicular to their line of sight to remove them safely.

GOAL: Guide the shrinking beam to destroy the ring and blocks within the action limit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the beam, shrinking it; mouse clicks set the firing pattern. RULE: Green blocks refill the action budget, extending your playtime significantly. TRAP: Misreading the beam's facing direction based on its trailing segment causes missed shots.

GOAL: Match the target grid's color pattern by stamping tiles. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the tool, clicks apply specific colors, space pushes the current color. RULE: Orientation dictates the stamp's shape, so align the tool before applying each color. TRAP: Assuming rotations are independent of position wastes moves; plan the tool's final angle before stamping.

ESTABLISHED: Orange growth pushes Pink down; Pink extends downward. Blue expands Red horizontally. Red shrinks vertically. Sky grows to reach target. FAILED: One Blue grow leaves Red overlapping the vertical block during descent. GOAL IS NOT: Simply maximizing all block sizes without checking for vertical collisions in the lower rows. CONTROLS: Orange and Sky grow. Pink grows via Orange pushes. Blue grows Red. Red shrinks.

GOAL: Fit the cross and zigzag into the top zone while adjusting the dividers to clear their paths. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece one block; clicks select a piece or divider. RULE: Every block has a dot, and reflections appear only where the piece stays inside the board. TRAP: Thinking dots mark empty holes; they actually mark solid blocks, so moving blindly caused collisions.

ESTABLISHED: The socket slides until blocked by solid walls. The wall is solid and currently blocks all valid slide paths to the target. FAILED: Right and up slides from the starting position fail to reach the goal; the socket stops at the wall or goes off-board. GOAL IS NOT: A simple straight-line slide from the current position. CONTROLS: Edge codes trigger directional slides. The middle row codes likely affect the wall’s position or state.

ESTABLISHED: The board has an M-shape with a central gap at row 12. Jumps remove the middle peg. Cart movement and jumping cost actions. FAILED: Assuming standard adjacency across the central gap. Treating the gap as a bridge for jumps between left and right sides. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the cart to the exit or filling all slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cart. Space jumps over an adjacent peg into an empty slot, removing the jumped peg.

GOAL: Guide the enlarged block to the top handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; panels trigger growth and teleportation. RULE: The block always leads with its dark side, extending forward as it grows. TRAP: Assuming the block retains its previous orientation after teleporting; it keeps its facing, requiring you to steer before moving.

ESTABLISHED: The rope connects to a box currently at rows 36-41. A target block sits at columns 48-51. The action budget remains sufficient. FAILED: Moving the box down and pushing the rope right did not automatically mark the target or clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply pushing the rope right until it stops; the rope must be positioned adjacent to the target, not just against a wall. CONTROLS: Right presses move the rope front; Left presses retract it to column 12. Up and Down move the rope vertically.

ESTABLISHED: The camera scrolls in fixed increments. The player occupies a three-column width. A ceiling blocks upward movement at specific row heights. FAILED: Clicking corridor blocks without moving right first left the player stuck against overhead obstacles. Attempting to rise through narrow one-column gaps failed due to player width. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing the immediate corridor row or reaching the initial upper room without navigating the final vertical shaft. CONTROLS: Clicking removes blocks. Arrow keys move the player horizontally. The player rises automatically into cleared ver

ESTABLISHED: Full action names like RIGHT are required; single letters fail. The marker moves freely through open cells. FAILED: Sending short move commands resulted in no state change. GOAL IS NOT: Moving blocks blindly without selecting a marker first. CONTROLS: Click to select a marker, then use full-direction commands to move it.

GOAL: Park two markers in target zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected marker; clicks choose which marker moves. RULE: Only the active marker responds to directional inputs. TRAP: Assuming all markers move together; you must manually switch focus before each new path.

GOAL: Clear the path to reach the hidden pink plus sign high above. CONTROLS: Move left to align with the vertical shaft, then tap above to break the ceiling block. RULE: The player automatically rises through empty space until hitting a solid obstacle. TRAP: Thinking you can rise immediately; you must first move left to align with the gap in the ceiling.

ESTABLISHED: The HUD requirement turned gray after the arch destroyed a piece. FAILED: Moving pieces to avoid the arch did not restore the yellow target. GOAL IS NOT: Placing any piece; the specific yellow Y instance is gone. CONTROLS: Clicking empty space drains the timer; clicking near pieces moves them.

GOAL: Reach the yellow token across the gap. CONTROLS: Arrows move; buttons rotate bars. RULE: Rotate the bar to bridge the gap, then walk across. TRAP: Thinking you could cross without rotating the bar first.

ESTABLISHED: The chaser trails four steps behind and catches you instantly if you clear the guard's path. The guard lunges along its axis, killing anything aligned at distance two. FAILED: Removing the guard by stepping onto its cell leaves the chaser free to pursue and kill you. Attempting to lure the chaser through the guard's line is blocked by the level's topology. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the upper zone, as the guard and chaser create an unavoidable death loop there. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move you one space. The chaser advances every turn. The guard triggers on alignment.

ESTABLISHED: Slots 4 and 6 offer exact matches for several glyphs, while Slot X offers rotated variants. FAILED: Assuming a single global transformation applies to all slots simultaneously; brute-force mapping of independent slot transforms is required. GOAL IS NOT: A simple visual match without accounting for rotational symmetry differences between the offered and target glyphs. CONTROLS: Click a slot to select it, then click a glyph to assign; right-click to clear the current selection.

ESTABLISHED: The path from start to launch pad takes nine steps. Rotating the plus twice takes three. Launching and entering the box takes two. Total is fourteen, matching the action bar exactly. FAILED: A longer route via the top row exceeds the bar limit. Running out of actions triggers a retry on the next input, not immediately. GOAL IS NOT: Just reaching the launcher or rotating the piece without moving it into the final slot. CONTROLS: Arrows move. Moving into the plus rotates it. Entering the top edge launches you across the board.

GOAL: Guide two blocks to meet in the center corridor. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; clicks switch focus between blocks. RULE: Only one object moves at a time; clicking selects the target. TRAP: Moving blocks independently creates dead ends; you must coordinate their paths through shared space.

GOAL: Clear the level in six moves by pressing arrows to move directly to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: You must count your steps carefully; the level has a strict move limit. TRAP: Assuming you can explore freely wastes your limited actions and causes a failure.

ESTABLISHED: A light-gray block exists inside a wall, unique to this level. Current water heights are uneven. FAILED: Repeated button presses altered heights but never triggered the block or equalized all sections. GOAL IS NOT: Simply making all water heights identical across every section simultaneously. CONTROLS: Buttons shift water volume between specific adjacent bands, changing local heights without moving the wall block.

ESTABLISHED: The orange moves right. The black box activates when adjacent, causing the orange to flee left. The player moves via arrow keys. FAILED: Chasing the fleeing orange is ineffective as it moves at the same speed. GOAL IS NOT: Simply cornering the orange with the box. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player. Pushing the orange requires standing behind it and pressing the direction of movement.

GOAL: Clear two terminals by pressing them in sequence across separate attempts. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blue snake; Space records your path as a persistent ghost. RULE: A ghost parked on a terminal activates its linked piston, opening the path for the live snake. TRAP: Assuming ghosts vanish between attempts; they must remain to hold switches while you navigate the next step.

GOAL: Reach the exit while navigating past a stationary guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: You can only neutralize a guard by approaching it from the direction it is not facing. TRAP: Assuming any entry into a guard's tile works; entering from the front causes immediate failure.

ESTABLISHED: The five-block piece overlaps the target slot when centered; the three-block piece sits low and left; the four-block piece does not obstruct the upper path. FAILED: Placing the five-block piece in the middle columns blocks the rising ball; moving the four-block piece is unnecessary and wastes moves. GOAL IS NOT: Filling the first cup with the upper ball; the upper ball clears the first cup automatically without interaction. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move selected pieces; Space launches balls; clicking selects pieces; the five-block piece must shift four units left to clear the path.

GOAL: Guide two characters to meet at the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active character one step. RULE: Standing on a key opens its matching gate; leaving closes it. TRAP: You can move out of a gate even after it shuts, so don't wait for it to stay open.

ESTABLISHED: The crossbar cannot pass through gray cells; overlapping triggers automatic clamping of arm lengths. FAILED: Moving left at high rows causes the left arm to hit gray cells, shrinking its length unexpectedly. GOAL IS NOT: Simply sliding the crossing to the target coordinates without managing arm distribution constraints. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the crossing point; arm lengths adjust automatically to avoid obstacles, altering reachability.

ESTABLISHED: The chaser uses Manhattan distance to pathfind. FAILED: Positioning to create distance gaps failed; rectangular geometry causes persistent ties at key junctions. GOAL IS NOT: Solving via distance superiority, as equal distances are unavoidable in this layout. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. Chaser movement depends on unknown tie-break rules when distances match.

ESTABLISHED: Moving left from the right side triggers instant death. Rising through the central shaft is safe. The upper area contains hazards that kill on contact from one row away. FAILED: Clicking on the hazard objects does nothing. Attempting to traverse the upper ceiling horizontally results in immediate failure. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top of the shaft. Avoiding the ceiling entirely is not the solution. CONTROLS: Left movement causes fatal collision. Up movement ascends the shaft. Clicking hazards is ineffective.

GOAL: Align the plug with the hidden socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Clicks toggled directional switches and a central activation button. RULE: Only the switch matching the socket’s exact position triggered movement. TRAP: Assuming any adjacent switch would nudge the plug; only the correct alignment worked.

ESTABLISHED: The strip covers columns 6-11 when at X=10. The player position must remain within the strip's current coverage to act. FAILED: Moving right to position 12 while the strip is at X=10 is invalid because column 12 is not covered. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving right until the strip fails to cover the player's position without first adjusting the strip's location. CONTROLS: Right moves the player one step if covered. Clicking sets the strip's left edge to the player's current position.

GOAL: Push the player to the yellow token while managing a moving barrier. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; clicks toggle the barrier's position. RULE: The barrier must be fully orange to allow passage through the second bar. TRAP: Believing you can enter the second bar from the far right; starting from column 16 saves three crucial actions.

ESTABLISHED: The level allows 128 actions. A valid solution requires approximately 65 actions. The current recording is complete and correct. FAILED: Spending too many actions on exploration. The current remaining budget is insufficient for the remaining required moves. GOAL IS NOT: Finding a new path or extending the current recording. Any extra moves now will worsen the failure. CONTROLS: SPACE ends the recording and starts the final run. Do not move the character any further before pressing it.

GOAL: Insert the plug's shaft into the socket's slot to secure the piece. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the plug one step; rotation keys turned the plug ninety degrees. RULE: The shaft must fully enter the slot without the sidebars hitting the socket's rim. TRAP: Assuming the slot was vertical; rotating the plug revealed the opening faced upward.

GOAL: Guide the pink tip to the center dot by clearing the orange's path. CONTROLS: Click the orange icon to shrink it; click the pink icon to extend it. RULE: Shrinking the orange creates space for the pink to descend through the grid. TRAP: Assuming the pink's length is unlimited; it actually stops if it hits a block or limit.

GOAL: Align the plug with the socket using a six-step program. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle direction and size steps; press to run the sequence. RULE: Shrinking the plug reduces its step size, allowing precise alignment impossible at full scale. TRAP: Believing clicks load presets; the grid manually defines each step, requiring exact configuration.

GOAL: Guide the sliding block into the target zone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; rotations adjust its orientation. RULE: Each move consumes two units of the shrinking energy bar, limiting your total steps. TRAP: Assuming the bar decreases by four units per move leads to underestimating your remaining actions.

GOAL: Connect matching color pins by moving plugs and sockets into alignment. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; clicking selects a piece. RULE: Only unconnected pieces can be selected; merged pieces lock until separated. TRAP: Believing free pieces are always selectable; once a piece is logically merged, it cannot be clicked, requiring you to break the connection from the other side.

GOAL: Extend the yellow arm to reach the target height. CONTROLS: Click to grow the yellow arm by three units. RULE: The arm grows upward while adjacent arms expand horizontally into empty space. TRAP: Assuming all arms grow simultaneously; only the clicked arm changes size.

GOAL: Align two sockets into one assembly, then fit a plug into the remaining pin. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active piece; Space rotates it; clicks select pieces. RULE: Pieces can overlap visually, but a merge only counts when pins align perfectly without overlap. TRAP: Thinking overlap was impossible caused wasted time trying to route around blocks instead of stacking them.

GOAL: Fit the four-row plug into the cavity by growing it and moving it down without hitting walls. CONTROLS: Dash and stem switches in one column combine to move the plug down and grow it. RULE: All six switches in a single column act as one command, not separate steps. TRAP: Assuming only the dash or stem matters causes you to miss the combined growth-and-move command.

GOAL: Reach the plus sign at the top of the map. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; clicks remove obstacles. RULE: The world has a solid ceiling, preventing upward escape. TRAP: Believing you could climb higher than the visible boundary.

GOAL: Align the cross to cover target points by stretching its arms. CONTROLS: Arrows move the center; holding a direction stretches the arms in that axis. RULE: The cross stretches in opposite directions simultaneously, creating a lag between arm ends and center. TRAP: Assuming arms move uniformly with the center; they actually lag, requiring precise stop timing to avoid overshooting.

GOAL: Clear the board by reducing all pegs to a single survivor through sequential jumps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved carts to position the board; clicks selected a source peg and destination. RULE: Pegs only jump over adjacent pegs into empty spaces, removing the jumped piece. TRAP: Assuming all key presses moved every cart; one cart often reached an edge and stopped, wasting clicks.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow goal is in a sealed region unreachable by walking. Teleport endpoints exist but are not inside the goal zone. FAILED: Walking to the goal. Teleporting directly to the goal. Moving tokens to the goal. GOAL IS NOT: A location the player can simply walk or teleport into directly. CONTROLS: Teleport swaps positions between token pads. Other buttons shift rows or swap patterns but do not open the sealed area.

GOAL: Navigate the plug to the socket using a six-step program. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle direction symbols; press Run to execute the sequence. RULE: Each column defines one movement step, so the final column must match the empty space. TRAP: Assuming the plug resets to the start; it actually persists at the last position, requiring a new path from there.

GOAL: Match the logo color to the target icon to unlock the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; stepping on the mini cycles the logo color. RULE: The mini advances the logo through a fixed color sequence until it matches the goal. TRAP: Assuming the first color change solves it wastes time; you must cycle until the specific target hue appears.

GOAL: Retrieve the rope, pull the blue crate to the gap, and lower it to the bottom. CONTROLS: Left retracts the rope, Right extends it, Down drops the crate. RULE: The rope grabs the nearest loose crate; pulling packs crates tightly against each other. TRAP: Extending further after grabbing the blue crate wastes moves; stop immediately to avoid overshooting the target.

ESTABLISHED: The blue bar grows left, pushing the white bar left into free space. The sky bar is stuck against the white bar and cannot move vertically. FAILED: Growing the orange bar right failed, likely because it blocked the necessary path or triggered a collision with player two. GOAL IS NOT: Placing the sky bar's dot on the socket, as it cannot reach the required vertical position. CONTROLS: Moving the white bar down drags the sky bar; growing bars pushes adjacent obstacles.

ESTABLISHED: The ring-plug structure is valid and all connectors were used, yet the level did not clear. FAILED: The current configuration caused heavy body overlaps, which likely prevented a clean merge. GOAL IS NOT: Simply connecting all pins; the shapes must fit without overlapping each other. CONTROLS: Undo reverts single actions. Restarting the level resets pieces to their pristine, unmodified start state.

ESTABLISHED: The floor hole is only at the far left lane; the middle lane is solid. The player is currently on the right side of the upper room. FAILED: Moving left then right wasted turns without reaching the hole. Attempting to fall from the middle lane failed. GOAL IS NOT: To exit through the middle or right side of the upper floor. CONTROLS: Left and right move the player horizontally. Gravity pulls down when over a hole.

ESTABLISHED: Stretching requires a bar blocked by a block, not edges, which clip instead. FAILED: Relying on edge contacts to generate the necessary 9-unit stretch for coverage. GOAL IS NOT: Achieving coverage through simple edge-clipping or unblocked sliding. CONTROLS: Pressing directions moves bars; blocking against the central block creates the required stretch distance.

GOAL: Extend the green piece to the socket by growing it. CONTROLS: Click to grow. Orange grows cleared the path; green grows extended the tip. RULE: Passive blocks cannot be pushed, but attached bars move when pushed perpendicular to their length. TRAP: Believing all obstacles could be shifted. The orange piece had to grow first because the initial blocker was fixed.

GOAL: Guide the blue head to the green terminal while managing ghost recordings. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the head; SPACE commits a ghost and starts the next attempt. RULE: Every third entry into the toggle square flips the plug, allowing passage through the gate. TRAP: Assuming the plug stays retracted ignores the parity shift caused by the second ghost’s extra loop.

GOAL: Guide the rope front to collect blocks and pack them at the target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the front; pushing drags attached blocks, retracting pulls them. RULE: Blocks attach only when the front stops directly against them, not just by proximity. TRAP: Assuming adjacency meant attachment; you had to back away and re-press to lock each block.

ESTABLISHED: Arrow keys move all carts simultaneously along connected wire tracks. FAILED: Moving carts to coordinates other than the specific target dock does not trigger loading. GOAL IS NOT: Manually dragging cargo or clicking empty space to win. CONTROLS: Up, Down, Left, and Right move every cart in that direction if the path is open.

GOAL: Guide the dot past the purple barrier to the finish line. CONTROLS: Click colors to extend bars, pushing the dot and other blocks. RULE: Purple blocks are solid and cannot be pushed; you must route around them. TRAP: Assuming the blue bar could slide down through the purple gap; its width caused a collision, forcing you to shift the yellow path left first.

ESTABLISHED: The logo cycles through a fixed sequence of shapes, independent of the current state. FAILED: Assuming the shape transformation depends on the logo's current configuration or position. GOAL IS NOT: A puzzle requiring spatial reasoning about the logo's specific grid coordinates. CONTROLS: Interacting with the pattern cell advances the logo to the next shape in the predefined list.

GOAL: Clear the path below the player and shift left to touch the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player; mouse clicks removed specific blocks. RULE: Clicking blocks in the player's column causes them to vanish, allowing a fall. TRAP: Thinking clicks only affect visible tiles; they actually clear the vertical path needed for descent.

GOAL: Navigate a grid maze to reach an exit tile while evading a pursuing chaser. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step up, down, left, or right. RULE: The chaser moves after you, always choosing the adjacent tile closest to your position. TRAP: Assuming ties in distance break by a fixed order; they may vary, causing unexpected collisions.

GOAL: Move the blue unit to the ring without colliding with patrolling ghosts. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one square per press. RULE: Ghosts activate terminals on a fixed timer, opening the path only after their specific move. TRAP: Assuming you can rush the exit; moving too fast means arriving before the ghosts unlock the gate, forcing a wait.

ESTABLISHED: The player moves in three-cell steps. A warp exists on the left side. Moving left pushes an orange block. The block has a cap above it. FAILED: Simple leftward movement from the start did not clear the level. Random wandering wasted budget. GOAL IS NOT: Just reaching the left edge. The block must be moved to a specific position first. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green square. Moving into a block pushes it. Entering the warp zone teleports the player.

ESTABLISHED: Rotations pivot strictly on fixed caps, preventing translation. Yellow and green bases are capped; growth fails when blocked. FAILED: Rotating the assembly to shift position; growing yellow or green against walls; assuming the stem allows a sweep due to gaps in rows 31-37. GOAL IS NOT: A simple translation of the assembly or a vertical sweep through the central stem. CONTROLS: Rotate moves bars around their base caps; Grow extends tips but halts if blocked.

GOAL: Merge four falling shapes by aligning their pins to form a solid block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space rotates it; Clicks select a shape. RULE: Shapes lock only when their pins perfectly overlap with an adjacent shape’s edge. TRAP: Rotating too early leaves pins facing away, forcing costly repositioning.

ESTABLISHED: Guard removal is safe and possible within the budget; the orange movement is periodic with a period of 40 turns. FAILED: Standard state tracking failed because it ignored turn number, incorrectly pruning valid paths as already visited. GOAL IS NOT: A simple tile entry; a potential lunge mechanic from guards may threaten the goal if not cleared first. CONTROLS: Moves update player and guard states; orange positions depend strictly on the current turn count modulo 40.

GOAL: Align the floating plug with the exit gap by managing water levels to position it correctly. CONTROLS: Click the valve to raise water, lifting the plug, or lower it to drop the plug into place. RULE: The plug always floats to the surface, so its vertical position matches the current water level. TRAP: Assuming the plug stays centered horizontally; it actually slides against the nearest wall, requiring precise timing to exit.

ESTABLISHED: The player stops safely at rows 79-82 under the jellyfish outline, avoiding direct overlap with its body cells. FAILED: Rising directly through columns occupied by the jellyfish's body causes immediate death, and passing through one-wide gaps is impossible. GOAL IS NOT: A simple vertical ascent through the center, as the middle columns are lethal barriers. CONTROLS: Movement halts against solid outlines; sliding occurs along ceilings when space permits, requiring precise column alignment to avoid hazards.

ESTABLISHED: The chain must be packed tight at the left before pushing right to align all blocks simultaneously. FAILED: Attempting to manipulate the floating chain or using a complex nine-step sequence exceeds the action budget. GOAL IS NOT: To leave the chain extended or to solve the puzzle by pushing blocks individually without full alignment. CONTROLS: Undo restores the initial state. Two Right presses push the chain. Two Left presses pack it tight. One final Right press aligns all blocks to win.

ESTABLISHED: The bar drains 0.5 units per move, leaving roughly 20 actions remaining. The blue ghost moves when you do. FAILED: Attempting the full 26-move path in one go fails because the bar empties before reaching the socket. GOAL IS NOT: Simply surviving to the end; you must reach the specific socket location before the bar hits zero. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move you and the ghost simultaneously. Each move consumes half a bar unit.

GOAL: Align the final piece’s pins into the matching sockets. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the piece; Space rotates it. RULE: Rotation changes pin direction, not just position; match the socket’s angle first. TRAP: Assuming rotation preserves the same relative pin offset; it flips the geometry.

GOAL: Align two colored plugs to specific target zones on a scrolling strip by managing water levels in four adjacent bands. CONTROLS: Click pumps to raise or lower water heights in specific bands; click walls to move plugs to different bands. RULE: A plug’s position on the strip matches the water height of its current band; adjust heights to match target columns. TRAP: Moving a plug to a new band instantly snaps it to that band’s current height, potentially misaligning it.

GOAL: Guide the plug through two gates by matching water levels to slot positions. CONTROLS: Click band buttons to shift water between reservoirs; click pistons to move the plug through open gates. RULE: A gate opens only when the water surface aligns perfectly with the slot’s left edge. TRAP: Assuming water flows automatically between connected tanks; you must manually pump to adjust levels before moving the plug.

GOAL: Rotate the shape 180 degrees to match the target icon, then navigate to the exit box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; entering specific pattern cells triggers rotations or flips of the held shape. RULE: Repeatedly entering a rotation cell from the same direction applies that transformation cumulatively to the current shape. TRAP: Assuming a single entry suffices for a 180-degree flip; it actually requires two separate entries to achieve the required rotation.

GOAL: Clear the level in just two moves. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the cursor; other keys edit the glyph. RULE: Correct glyphs stay put; only wrong ones change. TRAP: Assuming every slot needs editing wastes time; verify before acting.

ESTABLISHED: L6 features a distinct 'b' dot goal, unlike L5's frame-only finish. FAILED: Assuming L5's top-row or adjacency win logic applies directly to L6's dot target. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the top corridor or positioning blocks adjacent to a wall gap. CONTROLS: Standard movement shifts blocks; pushing mechanics remain consistent with previous levels' physics.

GOAL: Match the row pattern to the target by cycling slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor; UP cycles slot value forward. RULE: Cycle UP until current slot matches target, then move right. TRAP: Assuming DOWN reverses cycle order wastes time; just UP to match.

GOAL: Match the yellow row to the target sequence shown above. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; UP cycles the letter in the current slot. RULE: Each slot cycles through a fixed set of letters until it matches the target. TRAP: Assuming the cycle order was random or linear; it was a strict loop, so pressing UP repeatedly was the only way to find the match.

GOAL: Merge the scattered pieces to form a final shape, then move it to the target circle while dodging the arch. CONTROLS: Click to move a piece toward the cursor; the arch pursues the closest piece automatically. RULE: Pieces merge when they overlap or touch; the arch always chases the nearest active piece. TRAP: Thinking the arch blocks all paths; it only threatens the nearest piece, so use the other piece as bait.

ESTABLISHED: The piston at (4,10) cycles, extending left to push the block to (4,7) before retracting. The block remains pushed even as the piston returns. FAILED: Entering (4,9) from (3,9) or (4,8) results in being pushed left to (4,7) if the piston extends during the move. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not simply reaching (4,9); it requires avoiding the piston's active extension phase. CONTROLS: Moving into the piston's path triggers a leftward push. Standing still allows observing the piston's cycle position.

GOAL: Set each tile to its target letter by cycling glyphs. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP advances the current tile’s letter. RULE: Match every tile to its specific required character to clear the level. TRAP: Assuming all tiles cycle in the same order wastes time; check each tile’s unique sequence.

GOAL: Cover the hidden sticker by aligning bars. CONTROLS: Click to rotate bars or grow their length. RULE: The sticker is only cleared when every cell is fully painted over. TRAP: Assuming a bar's visible color confirms its position; the sticker might remain exposed beneath overlapping shapes.

GOAL: Slide the blue box left into the upper niche. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the box; clicks selected adjacent blocks to lift. RULE: Click the nearest block to the left that shares a row with the box to hoist it up. TRAP: Comparing column indices against row indices to find overlaps, causing failed selection attempts.

GOAL: Guide the piece to the target circle without being caught. CONTROLS: Click to move the piece or shift the arch. RULE: The arch only strikes if its path overlaps the piece's square; a single gap is safe. TRAP: Believing you need a two-square buffer, causing you to waste moves creating unnecessary distance.

ESTABLISHED: Growing orange moves sky up; shrinking orange reduces size. Red bar anchor is fixed. FAILED: Pressing "+" cycles arms without changing center color or triggering win. Rotating plus does not alter center. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the initial yellow center to the blue decal via simple rotation. CONTROLS: "+" rotates arms. Orange "grow" moves sky. Orange "shrink" reduces size. Red "grow" tests anchor behavior.

ESTABLISHED: Budget is 64 actions. Box starts at ceiling cols 20-22. Flipper A is at rows 31-35, cols 37-41. FAILED: Previous full-budget attempts depleted without clearing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the box to the shaft or triggering the reset. CONTROLS: RIGHT moves box +2 cols. MOUSE click on Flipper A reverses gravity, causing the box to fall down the shaft.

GOAL: Raise the block to the target circle while avoiding the moving arch. CONTROLS: Click the block to lift it one step upward. RULE: Vertical movement passes safely through obstacles that would destroy horizontal contact. TRAP: Assuming the arch blocks all paths; it only degrades the piece if approached from the side, not from below.

GOAL: Move the block three steps to the right. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the block; wait actions pause time. RULE: The block only moves when its color matches the current phase. TRAP: Believing color changes every action; it actually shifts slowly over real time.

ESTABLISHED: The plus token sits in row one, directly above its socket. A solid band separates them, blocking all direct paths. No downward beams currently cross this barrier. FAILED: Clicking the plus made it controllable, but it still cannot pass through the upper band. No existing beam aligns to transport it downward. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clicking the plus to win, nor manually driving it through the solid band without a transport mechanism. CONTROLS: Clicking a block makes it the active player. Unmoved blocks remain static.

ESTABLISHED: Pieces rise one step per move. Arches hit only when rows and columns overlap. Pieces move faster than arches horizontally. FAILED: Clicking outside the piece's current row band causes no movement. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the circle's column range while ignoring vertical alignment. CONTROLS: Click inside the piece's row to move. Use the top edge of the band to maximize upward gain while dodging.

GOAL: Clear the level by placing all boxes into designated spots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; the spacebar drops a held box. RULE: Chasers automatically move to capture fleeing entities, settling on empty cells once the target is caught or blocked. TRAP: Assuming a box can be dropped from any adjacent side; the box only attaches to the east, forcing specific positioning.

GOAL: Clear the level in nine moves to activate the recorder and trigger the final sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the player; SPACE confirmed the recording slot. RULE: Only valid steps count toward the limit; moves into walls or off-grid are ignored. TRAP: Assuming every arrow press consumes a turn led to wasted actions and confusion about remaining moves.
